summary.en: A fake real-estate agency that sold Taipei its own housing crisis — and helped pass a vacant-house tax.
summary.zh: 一間假的房仲店，把台北的居住困境賣回給大家——也推動了空屋稅修法。

en: Taiwan’s house prices are among the least affordable in the world relative to income. Builders hoard newly completed homes during downturns and release them when prices rise, leaving properties empty while ordinary people are priced out. Working with the TSUEI MA MA Foundation, an NGO for housing justice, we looked for a way to put the public and policymakers in the same room.

We opened an imitation real-estate agency — named after “celestial dragons”, the slang for wealthy Taipei residents who know nothing of ordinary hardship — on Roosevelt Road near Taipower Building Station. Its windows and walls were covered in posters made from people’s real stories of buying and renting, and politicians were invited to serve as one-day managers.

Within a month the agency hosted eleven talks on housing justice, online and offline. At the closing event, cross-party legislators established Ours 2.0 in front of the Legislative Yuan; in April and May the government passed the House and Land Transactions Income Tax and a vacant-house tax amendment. Run on a zero budget, the campaign raised NT$400,000, drove more than 200 million related searches and over ten media reports.
zh: 台灣的房價所得比名列世界前茅。建商在景氣低迷時囤房、景氣回溫再拉高價格，造成大量空屋，一般人卻買不起。我們與推動居住正義的崔媽媽基金會合作，想找一個方法，讓大眾與決策者坐到同一張桌子前。
我們在羅斯福路、台電大樓站附近開了一間「天龍房屋」——取自形容不知人間疾苦的台北有錢人的「天龍人」。店面櫥窗和牆上貼滿由民眾真實買房、租屋經驗做成的海報，並邀請政治人物擔任一日店長。
一個月內，房仲店舉辦了十一場線上線下的居住正義講座；閉幕時，跨黨派立委在立法院前成立「Ours 2.0」。同年四月與五月，政府分別通過房地合一稅與空屋稅修法。整個活動零預算，募得新台幣 40 萬元，帶動超過兩億次相關搜尋與十餘則媒體報導。

summary.en: Circles that divide like cells until they become a body.
summary.zh: 像細胞一樣分裂的圓，慢慢長成一個身體。

en: Cover design for the Traditional Chinese edition of The Genesis Machine: Our Quest to Rewrite Life in the Age of Synthetic Biology by Amy Webb and Andrew Hessel — a book about how synthetic biology may change the way we feed ourselves, treat disease and define family.

Overlapping circles in yellow, orange and red behave like dividing cells, gradually assembling into a living figure drawn in a single continuous line. Several directions were developed alongside the final cover, from bold blocks of colour to a floating embryo, each testing a different balance between science and life.
zh: 艾美．韋伯（Amy Webb）與安德魯．海瑟（Andrew Hessel）《未來的造物者：從消滅癌症、設計嬰兒到製造猛瑪象肉排，合成生物學將如何改寫我們與全球生物的未來？》繁體中文版封面設計。
黃、橙、紅的圓彼此重疊，像正在分裂的細胞，最後以一條連續的線長成一個生命的形體。定稿之外，也發展了多個方向，從大面積色塊到漂浮的胚胎，測試科學與生命之間不同的平衡。

client.zh: Midcity Centre，與 D&D Creative 合作

summary.en: A historic arcade in Melbourne’s Chinatown, refreshed — and given a Chinese name.
summary.zh: 為墨爾本唐人街的老商場換上新形象，也取了中文名字。

en: Midcity is a historic shopping centre in Melbourne’s city centre whose brand image no longer matched contemporary shoppers or the market around it. We were asked to reshape its identity for today’s audience while respecting its long history.

After an in-depth study of market trends and competitors, and working closely with Midcity’s team, we positioned the centre as a fashionable, diverse and modern destination. The refresh covers a new logo and visual identity, the interior environment, advertising, and the introduction of a Chinese name that brings Midcity closer to the culture of Chinatown while clearly conveying its values.
zh: Midcity 是墨爾本市中心一座歷史悠久的購物中心，多年下來的品牌形象已經跟不上現代消費者與市場。我們的任務是在尊重它歷史的前提下，為今天的客群重塑品牌。
深入研究市場趨勢與競爭環境、並與 Midcity 團隊密切合作後，我們把它定位為時尚、多元而現代的購物目的地。更新範圍包含新標誌與視覺識別、室內環境、廣告策略，以及一個新的中文名字——讓 Midcity 更貼近唐人街的在地文化，也清楚傳達品牌價值。

summary.en: Three cans, more than ten bodybuilders: rotate to mix and match.
summary.zh: 三款罐子，轉一轉就能拼出十幾種健身猛男。

en: Meat floss is rich in protein and minerals, so this packaging targets customers who are passionate about sport and fitness. Based on a customer survey, we drew a cast of funny characters holding dumbbells and wearing gym gear.

A tight budget shaped the idea. The illustrations were developed to run across the curved surfaces of stacked cans, so the manufacturer only produces three types of packaging while customers can create more than ten combinations by rotating them. The stacks make an eye-catching display in store, and a card inside lists the ingredients clearly. Compared with a conventional range, the design is expected to save about 63 per cent in costs.
zh: 肉鬆富含蛋白質與礦物質，因此這次鎖定熱愛運動與健身的消費者。根據問卷調查，我們畫了一群拿著啞鈴、穿著運動服的逗趣角色。
有限的預算反而成了點子的來源：插畫沿著堆疊罐身的曲面發展，廠商只需生產三款包裝，消費者旋轉罐子就能組合出十種以上的造型。堆疊起來在店頭也很搶眼，盒內附卡清楚列出成分。與傳統做法相比，預計可節省約 63% 的成本。

summary.en: Temple craft, turned up loud.
summary.zh: 把廟宇工藝的音量開到最大。

en: A poster series that brings traditional Taiwanese craft objects into a contemporary visual language. Rendered in saturated orange, ultramarine and magenta and wrapped in hand-drawn lettering, familiar temple and folk objects are reframed as something bold, playful and worth carrying forward.
A second set extends the series under the line “Move Taiwan”.
zh: 一組把台灣傳統工藝物件帶進當代視覺語言的海報。飽和的橘、群青與桃紅，加上手寫字體的包圍，讓熟悉的廟宇與民俗物件被重新看見——大膽、好玩，而且值得被傳下去。
第二組以「Move Taiwan」為標語延伸整個系列。

summary.en: A whole zoo drawn from the oldest Chinese writing.
summary.zh: 用最古老的漢字，畫出一整座動物園。

en: This identity for Taipei Zoo is inspired by oracle bone script, the earliest form of Chinese writing — an image record of how our ancestors saw the world. The symbol is transformed from the oracle bone character for “animal”, and the system extends the same logic to animals, plants and the zoo environment.

Because the ancient characters are already pictures, the system can keep growing: the staff and media passes, for example, are drawn from the characters for “person” (人) and “big” (大), both depicting a human figure. The work includes guide signs, a redesigned map, reusable sticker tickets that adults and children assemble themselves, and souvenirs such as silk-screened T-shirts and backpacks in bright red, yellow, green and blue.
Animal and facility signs, the guide map and environmental graphics — from building walls to elevator doors — share one vocabulary, so the whole zoo reads as a single illustrated world.
zh: 這套臺北市立動物園識別以甲骨文為靈感——那是最早的漢字，也是先人看世界的影像紀錄。標誌由甲骨文的「動物」轉化而來，系統再以同樣的邏輯延伸到動物、植物與園區環境。
古文字本身就是圖，所以系統能一直長下去：例如工作人員與媒體證，取自同樣描繪人形的「人」與「大」。整套設計包含指標、重新設計的導覽地圖、大人小孩都能自己拼貼的貼紙門票，以及以絹印印上紅、黃、綠、藍的 T 恤與背包等紀念品。
動物與設施標示、導覽地圖到建築牆面、電梯門的環境圖像，都使用同一套語彙，讓整座動物園像一個完整的插畫世界。

summary.en: One swollen, rubbery character, in every colour it could take.
summary.zh: 一個膨脹、有彈性的字，換上所有它撐得住的顏色。

en: A typographic poster series for “Nice! Nice!”, a one-day art museum event. A single swollen, rubbery character is drawn large enough to fill the sheet, then repeated, cropped and recoloured — black, green, cyan, navy and magenta — so that one letterform becomes a whole family of posters.
The small line set beside it, “Everything will be better”, carries the mood of the series.
zh: 為一日美術館活動「Nice! Nice!」設計的字體海報系列。一個膨脹、有彈性的字被放大到填滿整張紙，再經過重複、裁切與換色——黑、綠、青、藏青與桃紅——讓一個字形長成一整個海報家族。
旁邊一行小字「Everything will be better」，就是這組海報的心情。

summary.en: Two rings that keep crossing, until the conflict goes back to zero.
summary.zh: 兩個不斷交錯的圓，直到衝突歸零。

en: Cover design for the Traditional Chinese edition of Jayson Gaddis’s Getting to Zero: How to Work Through Conflict in Your High-Stakes Relationships.

Interlocking cyan and orange rings stand for two people caught in a loop, while the title characters 衝突 (conflict) fade into embossed white and 歸零 (back to zero) stays solid. Alternative directions explored counting down, scattered shapes and bright circles in blue and yellow.
zh: 傑森．蓋迪斯（Jayson Gaddis）《衝突歸零：如何化解重要人際關係的衝突》繁體中文版封面設計。
青色與橘色的圓環互相交扣，像兩個人困在循環裡；書名的「衝突」退成白色壓紋，「歸零」則保持清楚。另外也發展了倒數、散落形狀、藍黃圓點等不同方向。

client.en: Unify Hospitality Solutions, with D&D Creative
client.zh: Unify Hospitality Solutions，與 D&D Creative 合作

summary.en: A parent brand designed to stay in the background.
summary.zh: 一個刻意退居幕後的母品牌。

en: UNIFY is a hospitality management company that operates behind the scenes. It wanted a corporate identity that would quietly complement its subsidiary brands without overshadowing them.

The identity is built from the company’s initials — U, H and S — expressing its character and sense of stability in the simplest form. Scaled up, the three letters become supporting graphics that instantly signal a venue’s connection to the group.
zh: UNIFY 是一家在幕後運作的餐旅管理公司，希望企業識別能低調地襯托旗下品牌，而不是搶走它們的光彩。
識別以公司名稱的字首 U、H、S 為基礎，用最簡單的形式表現它的個性與穩定感；三個字母放大後也能成為輔助圖形，讓人一眼看出場館與集團的關係。

summary.en: Malt beverage bottles, dressed like royalty.
summary.zh: 穿上貴族禮服的麥芽飲料。

en: Power Malt is a malt beverage produced by a brewery with Danish royal approval and sold around the world. The bottle design is inspired by noble dress, bringing a sense of ceremony to an everyday drink.

The outer box is drawn as a sketch of a palace, deliberately draft-like so that the dressed bottles inside stand out. A book-like tag carries the nutrition facts and reinforces the noble style, and a derivative series explores the same idea through Chinese culture.
zh: Power Malt 是一款經丹麥皇室認可的酒廠所生產、行銷全球的麥芽飲料。瓶身設計以貴族服飾為靈感，為日常飲品帶來一點儀式感。
外盒畫成宮殿的速寫，刻意保留草稿感，好讓盒內盛裝打扮的瓶子更突出；書本造型的吊牌標示營養成分，也強化貴族風格。另外也以中華文化為主題，發展了衍生系列。

summary.en: Two textile artists, tied together by one knot.
summary.zh: 兩位織品藝術家，被一個結繫在一起。

en: An identity for “Woven Stories”, an exhibition imagined around the textile artists Anni Albers and Lucy Simpson. The concept uses thread and the knot to stand for both artists’ challenges and identities as women working in textiles.
A single orange knot becomes the logo and the thread that runs across posters, tote bags, umbrellas, coffee cups, wayfinding and the exhibition catalogue.

一個橘色的結成為標誌，也像一條線，貫穿海報、托特包、雨傘、咖啡杯、指標與展覽專刊。

summary.en: Animals drawn the way oracle bone script draws the world.
summary.zh: 用甲骨文看世界的方式，畫動物。

en: The Chinese Character Festival was developed alongside a renewal of Taipei Zoo’s visual identity. The project introduces Chinese culture through the relationship between animals and ancient character forms, using guided interpretation and interactive activities to connect language, image and observation.

Oracle bone script often transforms recognisable objects into simplified pictographic forms. Characters such as sun (日) and moon (月) demonstrate how physical forms can gradually become abstract visual signs.

We applied this principle to animals, translating their characteristic silhouettes into a contemporary linear graphic language. The resulting identity creates a dialogue between ancient writing and modern visual communication, allowing visitors to recognise both the animal form and its cultural reference. Across signage, printed matter and interactive applications, the system uses visual reduction to make the history and structure of Chinese characters more immediate and approachable.
zh: 漢字動物節與臺北市立動物園的視覺識別更新一同發展。計畫透過動物與古文字形體之間的關係介紹漢字文化，以導覽解說與互動活動串連語言、圖像與觀察。
甲骨文常把可辨認的物體簡化成象形符號，例如「日」與「月」，展現具體的形體如何逐漸成為抽象的視覺符號。
我們把這個原則套用在動物身上，將牠們的特徵輪廓轉譯為當代的線性圖像語言。這套識別讓古老文字與現代視覺傳達對話，讓觀眾同時認出動物的樣子與背後的文化典故。從指標、印刷品到互動應用，系統以視覺的簡化，讓漢字的歷史與結構變得更直接、更親近。

client.zh: The Bund，與 D&D Creative 合作

summary.en: One oval for every shape of bao.
summary.zh: 一個橢圓，裝下所有包子的形狀。

en: The Bund is a Chinese fast-food restaurant at Queen Victoria Market specialising in dumplings, baozi and gua bao. Named after Shanghai’s famous waterfront, it serves tourists, students and market shoppers looking for a younger atmosphere.

The identity uses an oval to stand for the many forms of baozi — a shape flexible enough to build patterns, frames and illustrations. An off-white, pink and near-black palette keeps it warm, light and contemporary.
zh: The Bund 是維多利亞女王市場裡的中式速食店，主打餃子、包子與刈包。店名取自上海著名的外灘，客群是觀光客、學生與來市場採買的人，他們想要更年輕的氛圍。
識別以橢圓代表各種包子的形狀，能靈活組成圖紋、框架與插畫；米白、粉紅與近黑的配色，讓整體溫暖、輕盈又現代。

title.en: Bodhi and a Clear Reflecting Plane

summary.en: Two Zen verses, and a mirror with nothing on it to polish.
summary.zh: 兩首禪偈，和一面沒有東西可以擦拭的鏡子。

en: Posters for an exhibition on one of Zen Buddhism’s most famous exchanges: the verses of the monks Shenxiu and Huineng. Shenxiu wrote that the body is a bodhi tree and the mind a bright mirror that must be polished so no dust can gather; Huineng replied that there was never a tree, never a mirror — so where could dust fall?
Brush-written characters are torn, smeared and rendered in silver, so that the image itself seems to dissolve as you read it — a visual answer to the question of whether anything was ever there.
zh: 為禪宗最有名的一段對話所做的展覽海報：神秀與惠能的偈語。神秀寫「身是菩提樹，心如明鏡臺，時時勤拂拭，勿使惹塵埃」；惠能回應「菩提本無樹，明鏡亦非臺，本來無一物，何處惹塵埃」。
書法字被撕裂、抹開，並轉成銀色，讀著讀著，畫面像是要消散——用視覺回答「本來無一物」。

client.en: Tea1825 Pty Ltd (JSY Tea), with D&D Creative

summary.en: Torn-paper mountains and gold-foiled ornaments.
summary.zh: 撕紙堆疊的山，與燙金的聖誕飾品。

en: A Taiwanese tea brand with a branch in Australia launched its first festive gift box with a torn-paper pattern that mimics the layered silhouettes of mountains, using special printing techniques to bring out a sense of luxury.
A second box, for the Christmas season, draws on the ornaments of a Christmas tree, with gold foiling to create a festive atmosphere.

第二款為聖誕季設計，靈感來自聖誕樹上的各式飾品，以燙金工藝營造節慶氣氛。

summary.en: Real fruit, pressed straight onto the page.
summary.zh: 把真的水果，直接壓印在紙上。

en: FengCai is a Taiwanese dried-fruit brand built on seasonal harvests and handmade, traditional methods. The rebrand set out to give it a new brand spirit and more points of contact with customers, and to stand apart in a crowded market without losing its local, home-made sincerity.

Positioned between the classic and the modern, the identity pairs an elegant, fresh logotype with patterns printed directly from real fruit, conveying both the handmade process and the quality of the produce. The prints use low-chroma, high-value colours for a fresh, healthy feel, and the text colour changes by product so the range is easy to tell apart.
zh: 豐采是一個以四季收成與古法手作為本的台灣果乾品牌。這次品牌重塑希望建立新的品牌精神、增加與顧客的接觸點，並在競爭激烈的市場中做出區隔，同時保留在地手作的誠意。
定位介於傳統與現代之間：典雅清新的標準字，搭配用真實水果直接壓印的圖紋，同時傳達手作精神與水果品質。壓印使用低彩度、高明度的顏色，呈現清新健康的感覺；文字顏色依產品更換，讓消費者一眼分辨。

summary.en: An app for swapping skies with strangers during lockdown.
summary.zh: 疫情期間，和陌生人交換天空的 App。

en: Skywalker is an app for sharing photos and videos of the sky. During the pandemic, it encouraged people to share what they could see from their windows — clouds, light, passing birds — and to open a window onto someone else’s world.

Users create a paper-doll character, choose a direction with the compass and send their “skywalker” off. Skies can be exchanged through a small game, saved, answered with messages and browsed on a map showing where each one was sent and received. A postcard tool turns any sky into something to print and send to friends and family.
zh: Skywalker 是一個分享天空照片與影片的 App。疫情期間，它鼓勵大家分享從窗口看見的天空——雲、光、飛過的鳥——也打開一扇窗，看看別人眼中的世界。
使用者用紙娃娃系統打造自己的角色，用指南針選擇方向，把自己的「天空旅人」送出去。天空可以透過小遊戲交換、收藏、留言回覆，也能在地圖上看到每一片天空寄出與收到的位置；明信片功能則能把任何一片天空印出來，寄給親朋好友。

summary.en: Covers for self-help, writing and science titles.
summary.zh: 心理勵志、寫作與科普書的封面。

en: A selection of further cover designs for Taiwanese publishers, including Rangan Chatterjee’s Happy Mind, Happy Life (你要快樂，才能好好生活) for Zhitian Publishing, drawn with a single joyful line, and a three-volume series of writing-vocabulary guides with stacked-book illustrations in purple, green and pink.
zh: 為台灣出版社設計的其他封面，包括知田出版的冉甘．查特吉（Rangan Chatterjee）《你要快樂，才能好好生活》——以一條快樂的線條畫成；以及三冊一套的寫作詞彙工具書，以紫、綠、粉紅三色的疊書插畫區分。

summary.en: Six online lessons, drawn as the Double Diamond.
summary.zh: 六堂線上課，畫成雙鑽石模型。

en: Posters for a six-week online course I run for designers in Taiwan, sharing overseas practice through design thinking, human-centred design and visual identity systems.
The Double Diamond — a common diagram of the design process — is rendered as two faceted, textured cones that open out and narrow down, giving the course a single, recognisable image.
zh: 為我開設的六週線上課程所設計的海報。課程對象是台灣的設計師，以設計思考、以人為本的設計與視覺識別系統實務，分享海外的工作經驗。
設計流程中常見的「雙鑽石模型」，被畫成兩個帶有質感的多面錐體，一開一合，成為課程好記的單一形象。

title.zh: 包浩斯視覺實驗工作坊

summary.en: Images made without a computer: pigment, mirror paper and water.
summary.zh: 不用電腦做出的影像：顏料、鏡面紙與水。

en: A three-day workshop with Markus Weisbeck (AGI), whose work treats the act of recording as the subject of the image: the picture is made by colliding objects and materials in front of the camera rather than by software.

Following the Bauhaus idea that point, line, plane and volume can be extended into endless possibilities, I sprayed pigment, placed mirror paper and drew beneath water, photographing the physical changes as they happened. The resulting images later became posters for novels I had read.
zh: 與 AGI 會員 Markus Weisbeck 一起進行的三天工作坊。他的創作把「記錄」本身當成影像的主體：畫面來自鏡頭前物件與材料的碰撞，而不是軟體。
依循包浩斯以點、線、面、體延伸出無限可能的觀念，我噴灑顏料、放置鏡面紙、在水面下作畫，並把物理變化的過程拍下來。這些影像後來成為我讀過的小說的海報。

summary.en: Biennale entries, chrome letters and other things made between projects.
summary.zh: 雙年展投件、鍍鉻字母，以及專案之間做的事。

en: A running collection of posters made for international biennales and competitions, alongside self-initiated type experiments: chrome-like 3D letterforms spelling Forever, November and Infinity; a carrier bag that reads Global Warming; and a pair of hand-lettered posters asking “Do you see the woman or the merchandise?”.
zh: 一路累積的海報作品：為國際雙年展與競賽所做的投件，以及自主的字體實驗——拼出 Forever、November、Infinity 的鍍鉻立體字；寫著 Global Warming 的塑膠袋；以及兩張手寫字海報，問「你看見的是女人，還是商品？」。
